newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ BONDS END STRONGLY, NZ DOLLAR RANGEBOUND.
newsitem.headline: NZ BONDS END STRONGLY, NZ DOLLAR RANGEBOUND.

text.p: New Zealand government bonds took their lead from a strong close in the U.S. to end a thin Thursday session well-bid while the New Zealand dollar closed steady to slightly softer.
By the close the Kiwi had finished a lacklustre session slightly weaker at US$0.6414/21 after opening at 0.6421/28. The Trade-Weighted Index was at 63.91 from 63.89.
Kiwi bumped through a 0.6410-40 a range largely in line with movements in the Australian dollar.
Domestic retail sales data, due on Friday, may provide direction for both the currency and fixed interest markets, dealers said.
Likewise, key U.S. producer price and retail sales data may prove influential.
It was an uncertain start for the debt markets when the market opened to a weaker TWI.
While long bonds rallied quite hard on the back of firmness in the U.S., the short end tried to do the same despite continued weakness in monetary conditions.
"You've got to start asking questions - what is the RB's attitude to the MCI? It now does not appear to be what they previously stated it to be," said one Auckland dealer.
The bank's monetary conditions index ended at 711.37, theoretically well away from where it should be.
"Their stated attitude towards the MCI, I don't believe is in existence any more," he said.
The bank has said it would be happy with the index at 50 basis points either side of 825.
"We are obviously now a long way outside those bands," he said. "Conditions are a lot easier and the market believes they should be a lot easier... perhaps the RB is condoning that."
